summary: The board heard announcements regarding local events [17:04] and discussed an agreement with Brookline Interactive Group to support town media services [25:13], voting to authorize the agreement [32:10]. Members of the board and public reviewed Warrant Articles 15 and 16 concerning multifamily zoning [20:42], [34:16], including a motion to refer Article 15 [2:04:42]. The meeting covered articles proposing legal expense reimbursements for town meeting members involved in an investigation [2:11:27], [2:19:11], alongside proposed bylaw protections for legislative activity [3:01:40] and inclusionary zoning amendments [2:56:08]. A major portion of the hearing addressed the Chestnut Hill Avenue street design appeal, focusing on bike lane options, traffic safety, and parking impacts [3:34:55], [3:51:05], [3:59:46]. Finally, the board evaluated Community Preservation Act funding allocations for the Housing Advisory Board's rental assistance program [5:44:12], [5:48:27], and debated the scope of town investigation policies regarding elected officials and school committee members [6:18:21], [6:30:37].
